modeling elastomer stress/strain relationships under sinusoidal losing using fractional calculus and power series instead of decaying exponentials.

I know some of those words.

Basically when you cyclically load rubber and want to predict how much it deforms and the internal stresses, it works better to use a fractional calculus model (things like taking the half derivative) because the elastomer is somewhat viscous and its response depends both on the current state and the rate of change. Before these findings, people had empirically determined decaying exponentials were a good model but it didn't fit great. These fractional calculus models result in a power series as the solution instead and match experiment much better. They also make sense from a micro standpoint, at least when looking at non-crosslinked elastomers.
